**Group:** Radiolaria  ·  **Optics:** high-mag, low-mag

## Defining characteristics

An acantharian: a single-celled marine protist (Rhizaria) with a distinctive radial skeleton of (typically ten to twenty) strontium-sulfate spines that radiate from the cell centre, giving a star- or sea-urchin-like appearance, sometimes within a surrounding cytoplasmic capsule. Key features: central cell with straight radial spines in a regular pattern.

## Distinguishing from similar classes

| Similar class | How to tell them apart |
|---|---|
| **phaeodarian** | Phaeodarians have a hollow porous silica skeleton and a dark phaeodium; acantharians have solid radial strontium-sulfate spines and no phaeodium. |
| **chaetoceros** | Chaetoceros setae are two thin bristles per cell along a chain; acantharian spines radiate in all directions from one central cell. |
